title: Best UGC Platforms for Creators (2026): Who Can Join, Fees & Payouts Compared
excerpt: Collabstr, Billo, JoinBrands, Insense, Trend, #paid and Newcollab compared from their own creator pages: who can join, fees taken from your pay, how you get work and get paid.
content:
Best UGC Platforms for Creators (2026): Who Can Join, Fees and Payouts

There is no single best UGC platform. The right one depends on your country, your audience size and whether you want fixed-price briefs or to set your own rates. We read the creator pages of the main platforms in November 2026 and summarise what each one says about who can join, what it costs and how you get paid. Terms change, so check the platform's own page before you sign up.

Disclosure

This guide is written by Newcollab, which is also a platform for UGC creators. We describe our own product in the same format and only state facts the other platforms publish on their creator pages.

Table of Contents

1. Comparison at a glance
2. Platform by platform
3. How to choose
4. FAQ

2. Platform by Platform

Collabstr

A marketplace where you list fixed-price packages that brands buy, and brands can also invite you to campaigns. Joining is free and every profile is reviewed, with no published follower minimum. Collabstr keeps 15% of each completed order, so a $200 order pays you $170; brands pay their own separate fee on top. Money is held until the order is approved, then paid out through options such as PayPal, Venmo and Cash App. More detail in is Collabstr free for creators and Collabstr alternatives. (Source: collabstr.com/pricing)

Billo

Positions itself as a way to "turn UGC gigs into a creator career." The creator page says you must live in the US, Canada or UK and be 18+, with no professional experience or social media presence required. You browse offers in the app and apply; once a video is approved, earnings are credited and paid weekly through Stripe. Creators can name their price for add-ons such as organic posting and partnership ads. (Source: billo.app/for-creators)

JoinBrands

Open to creators 18+ in the US, UK, Germany, Australia or Canada, with no follower minimum. You pick jobs at fixed prices (the creator page says there is no rate negotiation), and earnings go to a wallet you can transfer to PayPal. The free plan keeps 20% of your pay; the optional Creator PRO plan ($49.95 a month) lowers that to 15%. The page advertises earnings "from $60+ per video" and "$100+ per social post"; treat these as starting figures, not guarantees. (Source: joinbrands.com/creator)

Insense

Stricter entry: the creator page asks for at least 1,000 Instagram followers or 500 median TikTok views with 1%+ engagement, plus a UGC portfolio in the app. It lists many countries including the US, Canada, the UK and much of the EU. You apply to campaigns and can negotiate pricing; payment is held by Insense and released to your wallet after content approval. (Source: insense.pro/for-creators)

Trend

Free for creators with no follower requirement, but the apply button says US-based iPhone users only. You apply to photo and video projects in the iOS app, upload the content (no posting to your own social accounts) and are paid via PayPal once the brand approves it. Note: soona acquired Trend, and Trend's creator applications now point to soona, with Trend campaigns supported through the end of 2026. (Source: trend.io/for-creators)

#paid

Better suited to creators with an audience: it typically looks for 10,000+ followers and 1.5%+ engagement. You set your own rates for content, posts and usage rights; collaborations include 12 months of owned and operated rights, and paid usage is priced per month. Payment follows a 30-day processing cycle. (Source: hashtagpaid.com/creators)

Newcollab

Built for aspiring UGC creators, with no follower minimum. The free plan includes gift lists from brands, a brand directory, a free UGC portfolio and AI-written pitches (3 brand applications a month). Pro ($19/month) adds Polly pitching up to 20 brands every weekday with follow-ups, every paid UGC gig in the feed (collected daily from several sources) and unlimited applications. Brands pay creators directly. See UGC portfolios from creators on Newcollab.

Newcollab takes no commission: brands pay you directly.

3. How to Choose

  • Check your country first. Several platforms only accept specific countries.
  • No audience yet? Start with platforms that state no follower minimum, and build samples.
  • Want to set your own prices? Look for platforms that let you negotiate or set rates, and pitch brands directly too.
  • Use more than one. Most UGC creators combine a platform or two with direct pitching.
  • Bring your own portfolio. A portfolio link works on every platform and in every pitch: build one free.

New to UGC? Start with how to become a UGC creator and UGC jobs for beginners.

One Portfolio for Every Platform

Publish your samples and rates once, and use the link on every platform and pitch.

Build My Free UGC Portfolio

Free. No account needed. No follower minimum.

FAQ

What is the best UGC platform for beginners?

One that accepts creators with no followers in your country. Billo, JoinBrands and Trend state no follower minimum on their creator pages; country rules differ, so check that first.

Do UGC platforms take a commission from creators?

Some do. Collabstr keeps 15% of each order and JoinBrands 20% (15% with its paid Creator PRO plan). Billo, Insense, Trend and #paid are free to join; Upfluence and Aspire say they take no cut, and Newcollab charges no commission. Check each platform's current terms before you sign up.

Can creators in the UK and EU use UGC platforms?

Some. Billo lists the US, Canada and UK; JoinBrands lists the US, UK, Germany, Australia and Canada; Insense lists many EU countries. Trend's apply button says US-based iPhone users only.

Should I use a platform or pitch brands directly?

Both. Platforms give steady briefs and handle payment; direct pitching lets you set your own prices and build long-term clients. A strong portfolio helps on both.
